What differs: Damages between contracting parties and orders to pay the loss caused by misleading conduct in trade; fraud is also a crime.
Applies to any person acting in trade. The general ban on misleading conduct is enforced by civil orders, not as an offence.

Impersonation for gain is deception, and a false claim in trade that a person endorses or is affiliated with something is an offence. A free standing right to one's likeness needs judge made passing off, not read.
Use in trade. False claims in trade are an offence punished by fine.

Guarantees of acceptable quality and of reasonable care and skill, with damages from the supplier or manufacturer. Damages for personal injury are barred by the accident compensation law. There is no strict product liability statute.
A general privacy statute for agencies, with damages from the Human Rights Review Tribunal. An individual acting only in personal or domestic affairs is outside the collection principles.
The general collection principles apply to face matching and number plate matching. The Privacy Commissioner issued a biometrics code of practice in 2025, which sits outside the legislation site.
Civil liability with court ordered penalties for misleading conduct about financial products. Investment fraud is also deception under the Crimes Act.
Court claims for compensation for personal injury or death are barred and replaced by the state accident compensation scheme; only exemplary damages can be claimed in court.
Police only. Pretending to be a tax officer or other official for gain is deception under the Crimes Act.

Family name: Sexual images of adults without consent
What differs: Posting any digital communication with intent to cause harm is an offence. The intimate recording offence is written for recordings of a real person; nothing found settles whether a generated image counts.

Family name: Discrimination (race, sex, age and other grounds)
What differs: Government bodies and suppliers of services to the public.
Civil only. For public officials, candidates and matters of public interest the author must have known the statement was false or been reckless about it.

A general data protection law with a right to compensation in court, beside the general duty to compensate damage. The offence of unauthorized photographing (Criminal Code, article 202) is written for recordings made in private places.

The election regulation makes political entities name the commissioning party on campaign material, with fines. The Criminal Code election offences found (articles 209 to 215) cover blocking voters, vote buying, misuse of the vote and ballot secrecy, with nothing on fabricated media. The 2023 general elections law itself was not opened.
Use in trade.
A general duty to compensate damage caused by fault, and a contract made through deceit can be declared invalid; fraud is also a crime.
Traders dealing with consumers. The penalty chapter of the consumer law was not opened.
Liability of the producer for a defective thing, without needing fault.
Impersonation for gain is fraud. Two searches of the Official Gazette collection found no offence of impersonating a private person and no right to one's likeness as such.
Misleading advertising is prohibited, and making it knowingly is a crime. The rules protect consumers; the person whose name or image is used looks to the image right instead.
A person can stop the unauthorized use of their image and claim compensation, and attributing a false identity to gain an advantage or cause harm is a crime.
Fraud is a crime, and the Civil Code obliges anyone who causes harm by an unlawful act to repair it.

No law names face recognition. Biometric data is sensitive personal data that may be processed only with specific consent or on listed grounds, and the Constitution protects a person's image with a right to compensation. The data protection law began to apply in September 2020, after both incidents.
A person can ask for review of a decision taken solely by automated processing and for the criteria used. The article sets no duties on audits or impact assessments.

Family name: Rights violations by the state and its officials
What differs: Public bodies answer for harm their agents cause to third parties, without the injured person having to prove fault.
Negligence that causes harm must be repaired, with set heads of compensation where a person dies, and a public hospital answers without proof of fault.
Suppliers of products and services answer for defects regardless of fault. Whether a tool that ranks patients for intensive care beds counts as a defective product or service is for the court.
Note: The health regulator's rules on software as a medical device were not read.

What differs: Negligent homicide is a crime carrying one to three years in detention.
Deliberately causing another person moral harm is an unlawful act that must be repaired.
Harm to honor gives a claim for moral damages, and defamation is also a crime carrying detention.
The Constitution makes private life and image inviolable with a right to compensation, and the data protection law adds a duty to repair harm from unlawful processing.
Threatening a person with unjust and serious harm, by any symbolic means, is a crime, with a doubled penalty where a woman is targeted for being a woman.

Family name: Court conduct, false evidence and obstruction
What differs: Procedural fraud covers artfully altering the state of a place, thing or person in a pending civil or administrative case to mislead the judge or expert. Whether hidden instructions in a petition aimed at a court's software tool fit that wording is untested.
Note: The Code of Civil Procedure rules on bad-faith litigation and the bar's conduct rules were not read.

Family name: Discrimination (race, sex, age and other grounds)
What differs: Practicing or inciting discrimination of race, color or ethnicity is a crime, and a public body answers in damages for harm its agents cause.
Discriminating against a person on account of disability is a crime, and a public body answers in damages for harm its agents cause.
Whoever contributes in any way to a crime shares its penalties, and three or more people associating to commit crimes commit a separate offense.
A general data protection Act with compensation for damage, including distress, beside the constitutional right to privacy.
Any person; the remedy belongs to a consumer who entered an agreement.
False, misleading or deceptive representations are an unfair practice, with rescission and damages for the consumer. The Trade Marks Act was not read.
Negligence is judge made law in Kenya and no ruling was read. The statutory workplace safety duty stands in for records about harm at work.

Falsely representing oneself to be another person with intent to defraud is an offence, as is dishonest use of another person's unique identification feature. No right to one's likeness as such was found.
A right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, with a duty to tell the person.

Family name: Rights violations by the state and its officials
What differs: A statutory right to lawful, reasonable and procedurally fair administrative action with written reasons, giving effect to Article 47 of the Constitution.

The public health insurer has a statutory duty to pay contracted providers on submitted claims, and a provider aggrieved by a decision can appeal to a Tribunal that may reverse it. This is a statutory review route, with no damages rule in the sections read.
Note: The Law of Contract Act and the provider contracts were not read.

What differs: Advertising a medicine without the permission of the Pharmacy and Poisons Board, or with claims that it treats listed conditions, is forbidden. The Act is about advertising and licensing, with no product liability claim in the sections read.
Note: The Standards Act and the Consumer Protection Act rules on unsafe goods were not read.

What differs: A general duty on the occupier of a workplace; the offence sections were not read.
Defamation is judge made law; the Act adjusts it.
The general data protection principles and the right to compensation apply to face recognition. The special rules for sensitive personal data were not read.
Only the piece work pay and pay statement sections were read. Minimum wage orders and working hours rules were not read.
Pretending to be another person in order to cheat is its own, heavier offence. A right to one's likeness as such would need judge made passing off.
Damages between contracting parties; fraud is also a crime. Deceit is judge made law.
Suppliers dealing with consumers, and use of a mark in the course of trade.
Attempted murder and the general attempt rule, which needs a substantial step toward the offence. The murder, culpable homicide and hurt sections were not read.

Family name: Terrorism, weapons instructions, war crimes and hate crime
What differs: Detention or restriction by executive order to prevent acts against security, with no charge. The terrorism financing Act and the weapons Acts were not read.

The data protection Act binds organisations and gives a private right of action. The subject of a false statement of fact can get a court order to stop its publication. No general privacy wrong was found in the statutes read.

Family name: Rights violations by the state and its officials
What differs: The Penal Code offence of injuring a place of worship (section 295) was repealed on November 1, 2022. The religious harmony Act now carries an offence of urging violence on religious grounds. A planned attack on worshippers falls under attempted murder.
A general data protection Act with damages in civil proceedings. Processing solely for personal or household purposes is outside it unless it violates the right to privacy.

False, misleading or deceptive representations to consumers, and a false claim of sponsorship, approval or affiliation, are an offense. The Act gives no claim to the person whose name or image is used.
Note: The Trade Marks Act was not read.

What differs: Impersonation for gain is obtaining by false pretence. The Cybercrimes Act 2015 has its own identity theft section, and the official copy found refused the reader.
False, misleading or deceptive representations to consumers by those who supply or promote goods or services are an offense, with consumer redress through the Commission or the courts.

Note: Nigerian food, drug and product safety law was not read. On the third pass the copy of the Food, Drugs and Related Products (Registration, Etc.) Act on the site of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (nafdac.gov.ng) refused the reader. The Official Gazette would settle it.

What differs: Fraud is a crime with a minimum of 7 years. Civil deceit is judge made law and no ruling was read.
Fraud by a deceptive electronic message, causing loss by tampering with computer data, and phishing are offenses.
Note: The section on unlawful access to a computer was left closed.

Family name: Terrorism, weapons instructions, war crimes and hate crime
What differs: Knowingly giving support to a terrorist group, including training, information or material help, is an offense whether or not the support is used.
Aiding, abetting, inducing or procuring is punished under the terrorism Act for acts of terrorism only. The general rule on parties to offenses was not found in the collection.

The duty to reverse an unauthorized debit within 72 hours binds financial institutions and reaches debits the institution itself makes. It does not state who bears a loss when the customer was tricked into sending the money.
Note: The consumer protection regulations of the Central Bank of Nigeria were left closed.

What differs: Fraud by presenting oneself as another person carries a heavier penalty, and posting a created or altered image of another person that harms their reputation is its own offence.
Putting false or distorted data into a computer system dishonestly or by deceit, in a way likely to harm the public, is an offence. The consumer protection and trademark Acts were not read.
Fraud is a crime. The Civil and Commercial Code sections on fraud and wrongful acts were not read.
Putting false or distorted data into a computer system dishonestly or by deceit, in a way likely to harm the public, is an offence. The consumer protection Act was not read.
Defamation is a crime, heavier when done by publication, and an altered image that harms reputation is a separate offence. The civil defamation section of the Civil and Commercial Code was not read.
A general personal data Act with compensation regardless of fault.
Presenting oneself as an official and acting as one.

The access offenses apply where the system or data has a specific access-prevention measure. Damaging or altering data, disrupting a system and intercepting data in transit are offenses without that condition.
Note: The civil claim for a wrongful act under the Civil and Commercial Code was not read.

Family name: Sexual images of adults without consent
What differs: Posting a created or altered image of another person that shames them is an offence, as is putting obscene data where the public can reach it.

Family name: Discrimination (race, sex, age and other grounds)
What differs: The Constitution bars unjust discrimination on grounds that include age and lets a person whose rights are violated invoke it in court, with remedy from the State as the law prescribes. It binds the State and names no sum or penalty.
Note: Counted because the one record in this entry concerns a government cash program, so the State is the actor. No Thai statute on age discrimination in public programs was read.

What differs: No right against a decision made solely by automated means appears in the Personal Data Protection Act. Its data subject rights are access, portability, objection, erasure, restriction and correction (sections 30 to 36).
Note: Sections 1 to 90 read in the English translation on the site of the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society, through a reader that returns answers to set questions, and sections 31 and 32 read in Thai in the collection. Third pass, November 11, 2026.

What differs: Deceiving voters, slandering a candidate with falsehood and misleading voters about a candidate or party are forbidden ways of winning votes. The rule names no synthetic media.
Note: The penalty section of the 2018 Act was not found in the collection. The law library of the Office of the Council of State (ocs.go.th) would settle it.

What differs: Civil Code protection of privacy and image with compensation, and a personal data Act built on consent, enforced by fines and by a habeas data action. The fines are aimed at private data holders.
A general duty to repair damage; the national State answers under its own Act.

Family name: Rights violations by the state and its officials
What differs: Objective liability of the national State for irregular action, and an offence for officials who issue or carry out unlawful orders. City and provincial bodies answer under their own rules.
Capturing a person's image needs consent, with listed exceptions, and personal data cannot be processed without consent. No statute specific to face recognition was found.
Court decisions and administrative acts cannot rest only on automated profiling; such acts are null. Nothing found binds private bodies.
Injury to honor or reputation gives a civil claim. Insult and false accusation of a crime are offences punished by fine, but statements on matters of public interest are excluded.

Family name: Sexual images of adults without consent
What differs: The offence covers sexual representations of persons under 18. For adults no offence was found in the Code sections read; the civil right to one's image applies.
Threats are an offence. No national offence of stalking or of publishing private details was found in the Code sections read.

Family name: Court conduct, false evidence and obstruction
What differs: The record arose in Chubut Province, whose procedure code requires the judge to reason each ruling and bars delegating the judge's function. These are duties on the judge, enforced by annulment and by the Council of the Magistracy.
Note: The news service of the Chubut courts reports that on March 13, 2026 the Superior Tribunal of Justice reversed the annulment, holding that help from an AI tool does not by itself show that the judge delegated the decision and that nullity needs proof of real harm. It also names the Tribunal's protocol on AI use (Acuerdo Plenario 5435/2025), whose text and date were not read. The federal rules on judicial discipline do not apply to a provincial judge.

What differs: Deceiving a person into voting a certain way or into staying home is an electoral crime. The Code names no synthetic media. For a Buenos Aires City vote, the City electoral code has no deceit offense of its own and sends electoral crimes under national legislation to the City Electoral Tribunal.
Note: The Electoral Code of the City of Buenos Aires (Ley 6031, articles 254 to 266) was read on the site of the City electoral authority (electoralcaba.gob.ar), through a reader that returns answers to set questions: article 254 gives the City Electoral Tribunal first-instance jurisdiction over the electoral crimes set out in national legislation, and the sanctions title holds no rule on deceit or false information.

What differs: A general personal data law with damages and an offence for breaches done to gain or to harm, beside Civil Code damages for injury to privacy.
Businesses and manufacturers. Liability does not need proof of fault.
Death or injury by negligence. The dangerous driving article was not read.
Defamation is a crime as well as a civil wrong.
Fraud carried out with a computer made false image or voice of another person is an aggravated offence. Outside fraud, serious injury to a personality interest gives damages under the Civil Code.
Spreading falsehoods to sway an election is an offence, with a heavier penalty where a deepfake of the candidate is used, and a takedown route for candidates.
Damages for wrongful acts, and a declaration made because of fraud can be rescinded; fraud is also a crime.

Family name: Foreign influence, espionage, sanctions and export control
What differs: A heavier penalty where an election offence is committed on the instruction or funding of a hostile outside source. Espionage and foreign agent registration rules were not read.
Acquiring or using identifying information belonging to another without right is a cybercrime in itself.

Spreading a false, deceptive or misleading advertisement to induce the purchase of consumer products or services is an offense with a light penalty. The Act gives no claim to the person whose name or image is used.
Note: The Intellectual Property Code was not read.

What differs: A Civil Code cause of action for intrusions on privacy and dignity, beside a data privacy Act that punishes unauthorized processing.
Damages for fault or negligence and for fraud in performing an obligation; swindling is also a crime.
Civil Code liability for fraud or negligence in performing an obligation. The Consumer Act was not read.
Liability in damages for fraud, negligence or delay in performing an obligation.

Family name: Sexual images of adults without consent
What differs: The Act read covers sexual material of children, including computer-generated images. The photo and video voyeurism Act for adults was not read.

Family name: Child sexual abuse material and sexual harm to minors
What differs: Child sexual abuse material is an offence, and the Act counts computer-generated images made to appear to be a child.

Family name: False reports, hoaxes and false statements to officials
What differs: Publishing false news that may endanger public order is an offence.

Family name: Foreign influence, espionage, sanctions and export control
What differs: A registration and disclosure law for agents of foreign principals, with prison for acting without registering or for spreading political propaganda without filing it. It applies only where the person acts for a foreign principal.

The financial consumer protection Act makes investment fraud unlawful and punishes willful violations. It is aimed at those who offer financial products and is no rule on unauthorized charges to a card or account, so it is left uncounted here.
Note: The rules of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas on unauthorized transactions were not read. The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (bsp.gov.ph) would settle it.

What differs: No general privacy or data protection statute was found. Knowingly spreading false information that harms a person's reputation or privacy through an information system is an offence, with a removal route through the telecom Authority.
Defamation is a civil wrong with minimum damages, and knowingly spreading false information that harms reputation online is also a crime.
Using another person's identity information without authorization is an offence, as is knowingly spreading false information that harms their reputation. No right to one's likeness as such was found.
Publishing a false statement about a candidate's personal character to affect an election is a corrupt practice. Nothing specific to synthetic media was found.

Family name: Rights violations by the state and its officials
What differs: A High Court can order a public body to act within the law, declare its act void and give directions to enforce the fundamental rights. The clauses read provide orders and declarations and no award of damages.
Note: The National Database and Registration Authority Ordinance, 2000 and its rules on blocking or re-verifying identity cards were not read.

What differs: Spreading false and misleading news that causes consumer loss in electronic transactions is a crime, and so is creating or altering electronic information so that it passes as authentic. The general fraud article of the criminal code was not opened.
A civil suit lies against a party whose use of information technology causes loss. The general civil code rule on unlawful acts was not opened.

No identity theft or likeness offense as such in the laws opened. Creating or altering electronic information so that it passes as authentic is a crime, and using a person's data in electronic media without consent gives a civil claim. The 2022 personal data protection law was not opened.
The aviation law makes the air carrier liable for passenger deaths. The general civil code rule on unlawful acts, which would reach others, was not opened.
A business actor must compensate consumer losses from goods it produced or traded.
Causing death by negligence is a crime under the code now in force.
Note: The code in force at the time of the 2018 crash was the colonial-era code, which has no official Indonesian text on the sites tried, so the incident date reading does not count this entry.

What differs: Consent is needed to use a person's data in electronic media, with a civil claim for loss. The 2022 personal data protection law, which adds offenses and fines, was not opened.
Discrimination against a particular business actor is forbidden, and the competition Commission can fine it and order it to stop.

No rule names synthetic media or asks that it be labeled. Campaign material must give true, balanced and responsible information, a duty on those who campaign that carries no penalty in the regulation itself. The campaign chapter of the election law (Law 7 of 2017, arts. 204 to 329) holds no rule on synthetic media, false information or the likeness of a dead person.
False or offensive content sent online with intent to annoy, abuse, threaten or harass is an offence. The personal data Act was not read, and no general privacy statute was found.
Pretending to be another person in order to cheat is its own offense. It does not reach the use of a likeness where nobody is cheated.
Note: No statute giving a person a claim over the use of his name or image came up on the Laws of Malaysia site; that claim is judge-made law.

Family name: Sexual images of adults without consent
What differs: Knowingly sending obscene or offensive content online with intent to annoy, abuse, threaten or harass is an offence. The Penal Code and the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017 were not read.

Family name: Child sexual abuse material and sexual harm to minors
What differs: Knowingly sending obscene content online with intent to annoy, abuse, threaten or harass is an offence. The Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which is the main law here, was not read.

Note: The 2025 amendment Act (A1743) adds to section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act an intent to commit an offense involving fraud or dishonesty against any person, with up to two years in prison; that Act starts on a date to be appointed, and its page on the site of the Communications and Multimedia Commission shows no date of coming into operation, so it is left uncounted.

What differs: The Contracts Act reaches fraud between the parties to a contract and lets the deceived party undo it or be made whole. The wider civil claim for deceit against a stranger is judge-made law.
Falsely representing that goods or services are approved by any person, including a government, is an offense. The Act gives no claim to the person whose name or image is used.
Note: The Trademarks Act 2019 and the Consumer Protection Act 1999 are on the same site and were left closed.

Malaysian civil liability for intentional harm is judge-made law with no section to cite, and no ruling was read. The Laws of Malaysia site was read directly on November 11, 2026 and holds statutes only. The judgments of the superior courts on the judiciary site (kehakiman.gov.my) would settle it.

What differs: False content sent online with intent to annoy, abuse, threaten or harass is an offence. The Defamation Act 1957 and the Penal Code defamation sections were not read.
Threatening another person with injury to person, reputation or property is criminal intimidation, and menacing content sent online with intent to threaten or harass is a separate offense.
Note: The stalking section added to the Penal Code in 2023 was not found by its number in the reprint text.

Family name: Court conduct, false evidence and obstruction
What differs: A statutory committee has power over the conduct and discipline of judges. The Act read sets up the body and its procedure; the conduct standards are in a separate code.
Note: Filed with the actor as any person because the build counts state-only laws only for a fixed list of United States codes. The rule binds judges. The Judges' Code of Ethics 2009 did not come up in the site's list of subsidiary legislation, and the sentencing procedure rules were left closed.

What differs: Sellers, makers and service providers answer for defects regardless of fault, and unsafe goods or services that cause harm are also a crime.
Negligent serious injury, and unsafe goods or services that cause harm. The articles on causing death by negligence and on transport safety were not read.

Collecting or spreading a person's private life secrets is a crime, and moral harm from violating personal rights is compensated. The Labor Code bars an employer from deciding a matter that affects an employee on personal data obtained solely by automated processing, and requires that employees be shown the rules on their data.
Note: The personal data law (Federal Law No. 152-FZ) was not read.

Articles 10 and 13 of the consumer protection law were seen in the collection on the third pass; they concern wrong information given to a buyer and moral harm to a consumer, and do not fit a service misused against people who are not its customers. The advertising law was not opened. The official legal information portal (pravo.gov.ru) would settle it.

What differs: Court ordered refutation, losses and compensation for moral harm. The criminal libel article was not read.
Biometric personal data may be processed only with the written consent of the person concerned. The law states the rule and sends liability to other legislation, with no fixed sum per violation.
Collecting or spreading private life secrets is a crime. No separate stalking offence was found in the articles read.
Damages for a misrepresentation that led to a contract. The wider claim for deceit is judge-made law with no section to cite. Fraud is also a crime.
No identity theft or likeness offense as such in the sections opened. Posing as someone else to deceive falls under the fraud offense.
Anyone who aids, abets, counsels or procures an offense is guilty of the like offense.
The offense turns on a criminal or dishonest purpose in obtaining access to a computer. The separate offense of unauthorized access by telecommunications sits in another ordinance.

The personal information Act binds businesses that handle personal information and their people. For a private person the routes are the general tort article, which covers legally protected interests, and the offense of unauthorized computer access.
Damages under the general tort article; fraud is also a crime.
The general tort article, and a special rule making the person who puts a car into operation liable for death or injury unless he proves due care, third-party fault and no defect.
Liability for a defect in a delivered product that harms life, body or property.
Negligent driving that causes death or injury is its own offense, beside the Penal Code offense of negligence in the course of business causing death or injury.

No identity theft or likeness offense as such in the articles opened. Posing as someone else to deceive falls under fraud, and wrongfully making an electronic record of rights, duties or facts to mislead another's business is its own offense.
Unauthorized computer access is an offense, and so is making or supplying a program that makes another person's computer act against its user's intent.

Family name: Sexual images of adults without consent
What differs: The private sexual image Act leaves out images the person shown agreed to, knowing third parties would view them. Distributing obscene electronic records is an offense whoever is shown.
Distributing or publicly displaying obscene material, including electronic records, is an offense.
Infringing a copyright, or the author's right to keep a work unaltered, is an offense.

Family name: Foreign influence, espionage, sanctions and export control
What differs: No registration rule for agents of a foreign state in the code as opened. A citizen who helps carry out hostile activities against state security in the interest of a foreign state commits treason, and keeping links with a foreign state in order to commit treason, espionage or to set up an illegal information structure is its own offense.

Knowingly spreading false information that defames another person is a contravention punished by a fine or community work. The 2010 law on freedom of expression, which governs civil defamation claims, was not opened.
Unlawfully collecting or knowingly spreading protected information about a person's private life without consent is an offense. The civil rules on private life and personal data were not opened.

The Electoral Code bans campaign financing and material support by non-citizens, anonymous persons and foreign organizations. A word search of the whole Code on the State Register found no rule on synthetic or manipulated media, on false information, or on labeling such material; the election offenses of the Criminal Code and the Contravention Code hold none either.
Using an official capacity without right, together with an act tied to that capacity, is an offense. No general impersonation or likeness offense in the articles opened.

Family name: Rights violations by the state and its officials
What differs: The offense of hindering the free exercise of the electoral right (Criminal Code art. 181) is tied to listed means such as blocking polling stations, taking ballot boxes or violence. Deceiving voters with false media is not among them.
Organizers, instigators and accomplices are participants in the offense alongside its author.
Damages under the general tort article, and a contract made through deceit does not bind; fraud is also a crime.
Liability for harm caused by a faulty and unlawful act.
Insult, including attributing a concrete act or fact that can offend a person's honor, is a crime, beside civil damages for injury to personality rights.
Moral damages for injury to personality rights; violating privacy and unlawfully recording or spreading personal data are also crimes.

No identity theft or likeness offense as such in the articles opened. Fraud is aggravated where the offender poses as a public officer or bank employee or uses information systems, and unlawfully obtaining or spreading personal data is an offense.

Family name: Sexual images of adults without consent
What differs: No offense for sexual deepfakes as such in the articles opened. Unlawfully disclosing images or sounds of a person's private life is an offense, and so is publishing obscene images.

The election law punishes baseless rumors and propaganda capable of affecting free voting from 18:00 on the eve of polling day. It holds no rule on synthetic or manipulated campaign media; outside that window such media falls to the general offenses of insult and privacy.
Joint perpetrators are each liable as perpetrators, and helpers are punished with a reduced penalty.
The card law caps a cardholder's loss from unlawful use before notice, and using another person's card without consent is an offense. The payment services law was not opened.
A right of reply and refutation that does not depend on fault, and a court claim to protect dignity and honor.
A person's image may be shown or distributed only with consent; unlawfully collecting, using, spreading or altering confidential information about a person is an offense.
Unauthorized interference with information and communication systems is an offense, with heavier penalties under martial law.

Family name: Foreign influence, espionage, sanctions and export control
What differs: Espionage covers passing or collecting state secrets for a foreign state or organization by a foreigner or stateless person. The criminal code articles on collaboration with the aggressor state and on treason, which sit closest to acting for a foreign power, could not be retrieved.
Taking on the powers or title of an official, joined with any socially dangerous act, is an offense. No general impersonation or likeness offense in the articles opened.
Inducing people to buy or sell securities by false or misleading statements, and fraudulently moving the price, are offenses.
Note: Civil liability under the Securities Law was outside the part read.

What differs: Obtaining by deceit is a crime. The civil claim for fraud sits in the Civil Wrongs Ordinance.
Note: The Civil Wrongs Ordinance was not read: the Knesset legislation database (main.knesset.gov.il) holds gazette pages only, and no official consolidated text was found.

What differs: The rule protects consumers against a dealer who misleads them, in advertisements too. It gives no claim to the person whose name or image is used, and whether a stock promotion scheme counts as a dealer selling a service is for the court.

Note: The sections on wounding, grievous harm and attempted murder were outside the part read.

What differs: Assault is a civil wrong, covering both force applied without consent and a credible attempt or threat, with compensation or an injunction as the remedy.

Falsely presenting oneself as another person, living or dead, with intent to deceive is a crime. The civil rule on using a person's name, picture or voice for profit sits in the Protection of Privacy Law.
Note: The Protection of Privacy Law was not read.

Family name: Rights violations by the state and its officials
What differs: The Basic Law bars any government authority from violating a person's property except under a law that meets its limitation test. It states the right and gives no damages claim of its own; review is by petition to the courts.
Note: The 1958 law on reasons for administrative decisions and the Freedom of Information Law were not found in the collection.

What differs: Compensation and redress for a negligent statement apt to harm another's honor or reputation, unless the statement is justified on a weighing of free speech.

Family name: Court conduct, false evidence and obstruction
What differs: Parties must see that the case is correctly and fully informed, and lawyers must act in line with good lawyer conduct. The detailed conduct rules and the sanctions sit in instruments beyond the two sections cited.

Negligence is a civil wrong, and a death claim lies for the spouse, parents and children within twelve months. Whether a claim can be brought against a foreign armed force is a separate question of immunity that these articles leave untouched.
Depriving a person of liberty unlawfully, by force or by a show of authority, is a civil wrong.
Defamation is a civil wrong, with no need to show intent, and also a crime carrying two months to one year in prison where the injured person joins the case.

No privacy or data protection statute was found. The Basic Law treats any violation of the sanctity of private life as a wrong with no time limit and guarantees fair compensation. It names no penalty and has no rule on face recognition or biometric data.
Note: The 2018 decree-law on cybercrime was outside the articles read.

Family name: Rights violations by the state and its officials
What differs: An official who arrests or detains a person outside the cases the law provides for commits an offense, and the Basic Law makes any violation of personal freedom a wrong with guaranteed compensation. Mass identification of people by face recognition is not named.

Family name: Terrorism, weapons instructions, war crimes and hate crime
